correctness.rationale: If a set is not contained in one part and some part contributes at least \(k\) vertices, choose \(k\) terminals there and another selected vertex outside; the star through that outside vertex is a minimum Steiner tree and contains an extra selected vertex, so the set fails. Conversely, if the set lies in one part, every minimum tree for \(k\) selected terminals uses exactly one center outside that part; if each occupancy is at most \(k-1\), every \(k\)-subset meets at least two parts, induces a connected graph, and has a minimum Steiner tree on the terminals alone. The counting and maxima follow by disjoint enumeration. Fresh brute Steiner checks covered 49,944 candidate sets through order seven.
